title: Preview a Codex project installation
what: Deliver a mutation-free preview for installing one admitted pack on Codex from any directory inside a Git worktree. The preview resolves the exact version and selected closure, derives project-native targets, and discloses the proposed manifest, lock, notices, projections, requirements, and blockers without changing global behavior.
acceptance: The install command discovers one canonical Git worktree root and rejects invocation outside a worktree.
A dry-run for Matty on Codex reports the exact admitted version, complete selection, project projections, legal contributions, and intended project contract.
Human and structured previews are deterministic, redact sensitive values, and produce no project, Packy Home, host, process, or network effects.
Existing unqualified activation, update, deactivation, reconciliation, and status retain their global semantics and output contracts.
Stale observations and unrepresentable resources are reported as non-actionable before mutation exists.

title: Install Matty declaratively for Codex
what: Turn the approved Codex preview into a recoverable project mutation that vendors Matty's complete declarative closure and publishes the versioned project contract without staging or committing Git changes.
acceptance: Installation writes the human manifest, exact lock, mandatory notices, copied skill trees, and composable Codex instructions at project-native targets.
The lock is published only after every planned projection verifies and contains exact admitted provenance, graph, contributors, fingerprints, and modes.
Foreign non-composable targets, ambiguous Packy markers, owned drift, unsafe paths, and concurrent changes block before destructive mutation.
Unrelated dirty working-tree content and foreign content around intact composable contributions are preserved.
Faults either restore and verify the prior state or preserve a recovery-required journal; Packy performs no Git staging, commit, restore, checkout, or reset.
Repeated installation of the same intent is a verified no-op.

title: Verify and reconcile a project installation offline
what: Let collaborators and CI verify or converge the shared project contract from its manifest, lock, and vendored resources without requiring personal activation, network access, or catalog availability.
acceptance: Project status reports the shared installation axis independently from personal runtime activation.
Installed enforcement validates schemas, manifest-to-lock identity, closure, targets, modes, contributors, notices, and drift with a meaningful exit code.
The no-argument install command reconciles human manifest edits, regenerates an exact stale lock without floating versions, and restores only authorized missing bytes.
Status, activation, deactivation, and exact owned removal can interpret a supported self-contained lock offline.
Unsupported schema or minimum Packy capability fails closed, read-only status never migrates files, and missing bytes are never invented from a digest.
The installed enforcement path is demonstrably safe with sandboxed workstation inputs in CI.

title: Uninstall exact project projections safely
what: Allow a maintainer to remove one surface contribution or an entire project pack using portable lock ownership while preserving drift, foreign content, other contributors, and unrelated dependencies.
acceptance: Surface-specific uninstall removes only that surface intent and resources no longer retained by another root, dependency, pack, or surface.
Pack-wide uninstall removes all project intent only after a prominent complete preview.
Every removal target is freshly re-derived by the host adapter, constrained to supported project surfaces, and verified against exact lock evidence.
Changed or foreign content is preserved and reported as blocking drift; matching bytes without valid ownership are never adopted.
Composable files lose only exact Packy contributions and mandatory notices remain until their last dependent is removed.
Removal participates in the same recoverable transaction and never performs destructive Git operations.

title: Install selected resources and provider closures
what: Extend project installation from a complete Matty pack to explicit resource roots, transitive dependencies, native aliases, declared degradations, and deterministic capability-provider choices.
acceptance: Omitting resource roots installs the complete pack while explicit roots install their complete transitive closure.
The manifest stores direct roots, aliases, and provider choices; the lock stores exact resolved roles, chains, bindings, degradations, and provider versions.
Multiple valid providers require an explicit decision and no machine-global provider can satisfy the project graph.
Native name collisions block until an explicit valid alias is supplied; Packy never invents prefixes or silently duplicates a shared resource.
Every operational resource has a native binding or declared degradation, while dependency assets and mandatory notices follow their consumers.
Project contracts reject moving versions, arbitrary source URLs, machine-specific source overrides, literal secrets, and silent provider substitution.

title: Share project projections across Codex and OpenCode
what: Install the same exact project pack for OpenCode while sharing host-neutral project projections with Codex and preserving separate host-native configuration where formats differ.
acceptance: OpenCode receives complete project-native projections for supported skills, instructions, agents, commands, MCP definitions, hooks, and assets.
Codex and OpenCode use one physical project skill projection when both natively discover the same target and alias.
The lock records both contributors and adding a contributor does not rewrite an already-correct shared projection.
Removing either surface preserves shared resources until the last contributor is removed.
Divergent aliases for one shared physical target block instead of producing silent duplicate copies.
Incidental discovery by the other surface is disclosed but never recorded as installation or activation intent.

title: Install complete project packs for Claude Code
what: Add complete declarative project installation for Claude Code using its native project surfaces while preserving the same project contract, ownership, security, and recovery semantics.
acceptance: Claude Code receives representable project skills, instructions, rules, agents, MCP definitions, hooks, assets, and mandatory notices from the exact locked closure.
Project configuration contains only non-secret definitions and secret references; OAuth, credentials, trust, and personal settings remain outside the shared contract.
Claude-specific paths and structural merges are derived by the Claude adapter and constrained to the Git worktree.
Existing project content is preserved outside exact Packy contributions and collisions or drift fail closed.
Dry-run, apply, offline status, reconcile, and uninstall expose behavior equivalent to the already-supported project lifecycle.
Global Claude activation behavior remains unchanged.

title: Update one project pack across all surfaces
what: Deliver explicit project pack updates that change one exact pack version and reconcile every installed surface, selected closure, notice, and shared contributor in one recoverable transaction.
acceptance: Project update has no surface selector and previews all affected surfaces because one pack version governs the project.
Update changes the exact manifest version, lock identity, closure, projections, aliases, provider consequences, and notices without resolving ranges or moving refs.
A requested version must be an admitted catalog or history version and no per-machine source override can change its bytes.
Shared projections are rewritten once, contributor accounting remains correct, and host-specific projections change independently.
Manual projection edits, stale plans, incompatible schemas, unavailable exact sources, and unresolved recovery block safely.
Sensitive changes are classified and disclosed for later personal reactivation.

title: Activate sensitive Codex project runtime effects
what: Allow the current user to activate the exact sensitive runtime effects of a valid Codex project installation without copying declarative resources again or transferring consent through Git.
acceptance: Project activation requires a valid installed pack and never creates an implicit project installation.
Personal state, approvals, receipts, sensitive lock identity, and recovery live under Packy Home keyed by the canonical worktree digest.
Separate clones and worktrees do not share consent, moved checkouts require reactivation, and declarative-only packs report activation as not required.
MCP, hooks, plugins, external requirements, trust, and authentication are separately previewed and approved without persisting secret values.
Interactive install may offer the separately previewed activation, while non-interactive install never activates implicitly.
Usable enforcement combines valid installation, current personal activation, fresh authorization, external requirements, and observed Codex readiness.

title: Activate project runtime effects on OpenCode and Claude Code
what: Extend personal project activation, deactivation, receipts, sensitive identity, and readiness to OpenCode and Claude Code using their native runtime and trust mechanisms.
acceptance: OpenCode and Claude project activation consume their existing project lock and do not duplicate declarative projections.
Each host adapter exposes exact sensitive effects, pending human actions, authorization evidence, usability evidence, and reversible personal contributions.
MCP credentials, OAuth tokens, and host trust remain host- or user-owned and never enter Packy project artifacts or receipts.
Hook execution is bound to an immutable approved identity or freshly verifies the approved digest before changed bytes can run.
Project deactivation removes only exact personal effects and leaves the shared installation untouched.
Human and structured output use the same installation and runtime state vocabulary across all supported surfaces.

title: Compose global and project runtime state
what: Report and enforce the additive effective runtime state produced by global activation, project installation, and personal project activation without hidden host precedence or redundant consent.
acceptance: Exact compatible global effects satisfy project runtime resource by resource and are reported as inherited global coverage without creating project receipts.
Partial global coverage leaves uncovered project effects pending and global deactivation never activates them locally.
Incompatible global and project contracts, bindings, aliases, or sensitive definitions create an explicit activation scope conflict and block usable readiness.
Project installation remains valid and committable despite the installer's personal global conflict.
Sensitive project lock changes make prior personal activation stale and require a newly previewed approval before changed effects are enabled.
Purely declarative changes do not fabricate renewed runtime consent.

title: Clean up deactivated, orphaned, and recovery-required project state
what: Complete the collaborative removal lifecycle so personal effects, shared uninstall commits, stale receipts, and interrupted transactions can be diagnosed and cleaned without automatic authority expansion.
acceptance: Uninstall detects current personal activation and offers a separately previewed deactivation before shared removal.
Pulling a project uninstall leaves another collaborator's remaining receipts in an explicit orphaned state and performs no automatic cleanup.
Orphaned deactivation can remove exact personal contributions using preserved receipts even when shared resources are gone.
Drifted personal configuration is preserved and blocks destructive cleanup; receipts retire only after verified absence.
Unresolved recovery blocks new project mutation and the next install command handles recovery before new intent.
Status and usable enforcement provide exact commands and stable structured facts for stale, orphaned, blocked, and recovery-required states.

title: Qualify the complete project pack lifecycle
what: Qualify and document the complete global-plus-project lifecycle across admitted packs, resource kinds, and all supported CLI surfaces so the feature is safe to hand to users and delivery agents.
acceptance: End-to-end acceptance covers full packs, selected resources, shared projections, aliases, providers, updates, personal activation, inherited coverage, conflicts, stale activation, orphan cleanup, and recovery.
Human output, help, examples, and structured JSON contracts consistently distinguish installation from runtime activation and document the guided two-phase flow.
Published schemas and canonical negative fixtures cover project manifest, lock, status, preview, apply, failure, and recovery contracts.
Documentation explains Git workflow, offline behavior, secrets, notices, CI installed enforcement, usable enforcement, and global backward compatibility.
Architecture tests prove capabilitypack remains the sole semantic owner and host adapters retain projection representation ownership.
The repository validation authority, including race detection, passes without weakening existing global lifecycle evidence.
